name: Guinea-Bissau

facts.religion: Muslim about 46%, Christian about 22%, traditional faiths

snapshot: The army seized power in November 2025 on the eve of election results, the latest of many coups in a country known as a cocaine transit hub.
culture: Guinea-Bissau's Kriol, a Portuguese-based creole, unites some 20 ethnic groups. The Bijagós archipelago, a UNESCO biosphere reserve, preserves matrilineal traditions in which women traditionally choose their husbands. Gumbé music and the February carnival in Bissau mix Portuguese and African influences.
society: Cashew nuts make up most exports and employ much of the rural population. The country has had more coups and attempts than almost any other since independence from Portugal in 1974. Weak institutions have made it a transit point for South American cocaine heading to Europe.
situation: On 26 November 2025, the day before provisional results of presidential and legislative elections, officers seized power and named General Horta Inta-A, known as N'Tam, as transitional president for one year. President Umaro Sissoco Embaló left for Senegal. The junta has scheduled new elections for 6 December 2026.
power: A military transition. The junta's transitional president governs by decree with an appointed prime minister until the promised elections; under the constitution the country is semi- presidential, with a directly elected president and a prime minister answerable to parliament.

leaders.state: Transitional President General Horta Inta-A, since November 2025
